name: Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava Connecting Through Coronary Sinus to Left-Sided Atrium
aliases: Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava with Left Atrial Drainage
Left Superior Vena Cava to Left Atrium via Coronary Sinus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava

criteria.description: Visualization of persistent left superior vena cava draining into the coronary sinus and subsequently into the left atrium by echocardiography, CT, or MRI
Contrast bubble study demonstrating right-to-left shunting via coronary sinus to left atrium
Presence of unexplained hypoxemia or cyanosis without pulmonary pathology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of persistent left superior vena cava draining into left atrium via coronary sinus on imaging plus evidence of right-to-left shunting
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multimodal imaging and exclusion of other causes of right-to-left shunt.

pathognomonic.notes: Central cyanosis often present from birth or early infancy
searchTerms: blue skin from abnormal heart blood flow
cyanosis due to right-to-left heart shunt

pathognomonic.notes: Persistent low oxygen saturation despite supplemental oxygen
searchTerms: low oxygen levels not improving with oxygen therapy
hypoxemia resistant to supplemental oxygen
oxygen therapy failing to raise blood oxygen

pathognomonic.notes: Stroke or transient ischemic attacks due to emboli bypassing pulmonary filtration

common.notes: Reduced exercise capacity due to hypoxemia
Generalized tiredness not explained by other causes
searchTerms: tiredness from low oxygen levels
chronic fatigue due to poor oxygenation
feeling weak from long-term low oxygen

common.notes: Digital clubbing secondary to chronic hypoxemia
searchTerms: enlarged fingertips and toes
clubbing of nails
bulbous finger and toe tips

common.symptomName: Heart murmur due to associated cardiac anomalies

heart murmur caused by heart problems

occasional.notes: Atrial arrhythmias due to coronary sinus dilation
Multiple embolic events without clear source

breathlessness on exertion
difficulty breathing with activity

occasional.notes: Transient loss of consciousness possibly due to arrhythmia or hypoxia

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to volume overload
searchTerms: high lung blood pressure from extra blood volume

heart infection in coronary sinus area

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia with normal or low PaCO2
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating persistent left superior vena cava draining into coronary sinus and left atrium
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography confirming anomalous venous drainage
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; may be associated with congenital heart disease syndromes
other: Electrocardiogram may show arrhythmias or right atrial enlargement

distinguishingFeatures: Pulmonary veins draining anomalously rather than systemic veins
Shunting occurs at atrial level, not via coronary sinus
Often diagnosed with bubble contrast echocardiography
No persistent left superior vena cava present

redFlags: Severe hypoxemia unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Onset of arrhythmias or syncope in a patient with known anomaly
